works.title: Breaking water-structure constraints by Hofmeister effects in interfacial polymerization for polyamide membranes
works.abstract: Abstract Hydration critically governs the physicochemical behavior of solutes in both the aqueous bulk and interfacial environments. As typical chaotropic Hofmeister ions, weakly hydrated anions (WHAs) can reshape hydration structures and accumulate at water–hydrophobe interfaces. Notably, WHAs paradoxically suppress the solubility of certain small-molecule monomers in water while enhancing that of chemically analogous polymers. Here, we exploit WHA-mediated Hofmeister hydration control to regulate polyamide-forming interfacial polymerization (IP), using the piperazine (PIP) and trimesoyl chloride (TMC) nanofiltration system as the primary model. Introducing WHAs into the aqueous phase reduces the affinity of amine monomers for water and accelerates partitioning into the reaction front in the oil phase, remarkably reinforcing IP self-limitation. Simultaneously, interfacial WHA enrichment lowers interfacial tension and, together with accelerated amine delivery, potentially intensifies transport-driven interfacial instabilities. WHAs also lower interfacial water availability, attenuating acyl chloride hydrolysis. These synergistic effects yield hollow-ridged polyamide selective layers with reduced thickness and high crosslinking density, delivering enhanced water permeance and salt rejection. Crucially, module-scale fabrication of high-performance membranes demonstrates that WHA-mediated Hofmeister hydration control is directly compatible with established desalination pipelines.

works.title: Angstrom-Precise Vapor-Synthesized Polyamide Membranes for Ion–Ion Separation
works.abstract: Abstract Precise ion–ion separation using nanofiltration (NF) membranes remains a central challenge in water treatment and resource recovery. Conventional fabrication by interfacial polymerization (IP) provides limited control over the structure of the polyamide (PA) selective layer, thereby constraining ion–ion separation. Using a solvent-free, vapor-phase, layer-by-layer approach, we synthesized a PA selective layer for NF via molecular layer deposition (MLD) of trimesoyl chloride (TMC) and piperazine (PIP). This strategy enables angstrom-scale control over PA growth with a deposition rate of 1.3 Å per cycle and yields spatially uniform membranes with a mean pore size of 5.08 Å and a narrow geometric standard deviation of 1.18. MLD further enables precise control over surface chemistry through either TMC or PIP termination. Structural, chemical, and transport characterizations indicate an enhanced size-based exclusion and reduced Donnan exclusion in the MLD-grown membranes. MLD membranes with ∼39 nm-thick PA layer exhibited a water permeance of 13.0 L m–2 h–1 bar–1 and monovalent–divalent cation (Li+/Mg2+) and anion (Cl–/SO42–) selectivities of 36 and 92, respectively. This work establishes MLD-grown PA membranes as a model platform for precise PA structural control and mechanistic interrogation of ion–ion separation, providing design principles for more selective membranes.

works.title: In situ crosslinking of sulfonated polyphenylsulfone membranes via polyethyleneimine-glutaraldehyde chemistry for organic solvent nanofiltration
works.abstract: Sulfonated polyphenylsulfone (sPPSU) is an attractive material for organic solvent nanofiltration (OSN) owing to its hydrophilicity and ease of processing. However, its application in OSN is limited by insufficient chemical stability which is commonly addressed by blending sPPSU with costly high-performance polymers. In this work, a simple and cost-effective strategy was developed to fabricate chemically stable sPPSU membranes through in situ crosslinking during phase inversion. Polyethyleneimine (PEI) was incorporated into the casting solution to introduce reactive amine groups, which subsequently formed covalent crosslinks with glutaraldehyde (GA) present in the coagulation bath. A secondary PEI coating was further applied to tune surface chemistry and separation performance. By varying the molecular weight of PEI in both the membrane bulk and coating layer, membrane structure and separation characteristics could be systematically tuned. The densest membrane exhibited a molecular weight cut off (MWCO) of approximately 650 g mol −1 , a narrow pore size distribution of 0.5–2.0 nm, and solvent permeances of 16.4, 12.0, and 4.8 L m −2 h −1 bar −1 for water, methanol, and ethanol, respectively. Tetracycline rejection exceeded 95%, while long-term filtration experiments demonstrated stable membrane performance and structural integrity during 120 h operation in DMAc. Control membranes without GA crosslinking completely dissolved in DMAc, showing the critical role of the in situ crosslinking strategy in achieving solvent resistance. These results demonstrate that PEI, an inexpensive amine-rich polymer, can be employed to fabricate highly solvent-stable sPPSU membranes without the need for costly specialty polymers. The proposed approach offers a practical balance between membrane performance, chemical stability, and fabrication simplicity, making it attractive for industrial OSN applications.

works.title: Hydroxy artificial water channels enable ultraselective reverse osmosis membranes for N-nitrosamine removal in water reuse
institutions: Shanghai Institute of Pollution Control and Ecological Security
works.abstract: Reverse osmosis (RO) is a leading technology of water reuse for addressing global water scarcity. However, current RO membranes often struggle to effectively reject certain harmful small molecules in water and wastewater, such as N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA). Herein, inspired by the channel proteins in cell membranes, an ultraselective RO membrane (AWCM) was developed by incorporating hydroxy artificial water channels (OH AWCs) into the polyamide (PA) rejection layer. OH AWCs mediated the transport pathways, enabling the membrane to deliver a NaCl rejection of 99.2 ± 0.3%, an NDMA rejection of 93.9 ± 0.1% that surpassed the existing upper bound of permselectivity, and an ultrahigh pure water permeance (4.5 ± 0.2 L·m−2·h−1·bar−1) that exceeded that of state-of-the-art RO membranes. Within the OH AWCs, the hydrogen bonds formed between water molecules and the -OH resulted in a short residence time and a high jump frequency of water molecules, enabling the formation of dynamic and continuous OH-H2O networks that facilitated rapid water movement. In contrast, NaCl and NDMA faced high trans-channel energy barriers, which significantly hindered their transport through the OH AWCs. The resulting AWCM membrane outperforms prevailing RO membranes and offers valuable insights for the design of next-generation RO membranes. Low N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA) rejection by reverse osmosis membrane threatens the quality of permeate. Here, the authors created a membrane with hydroxy artificial water channels, improving water permeance and NDMA rejection for safer water reuse.

works.title: Oxygen Plasma-Activated PES Ultrafiltration Substrates for Constructing High-Performance Mg2+/Li + Separation Nanofiltration Membranes
works.abstract: Abstract Positively charged polyamide (PA) nanofiltration (NF) membranes hold great potential for Mg2+/Li+ separation, but their performance is strongly affected by the surface properties and pore structures of the substrate. In this study, a PES ultrafiltration substrate was pretreated by ethanol natural evaporation and then activated by oxygen plasma prior to interfacial polymerization to fabricate composite NF membranes. The pretreatment effectively suppressed irreversible pore shrinkage of the PES substrate during drying, enabling the E-PES-UF substrate to maintain a high water flux of 228 LMH. Subsequent oxygen plasma activation improved the hydrophilicity and interfacial wettability of the substrate through mild etching and the introduction of polar oxygen-containing groups, thereby promoting the uniform distribution of PEI aqueous-phase monomers on the activated substrate surface. As a result, the optimized E-30-20-NF membrane exhibited a uniform PA layer with a thickness of only 37 nm and an isoelectric point of pH 8.85. It achieved a Mg2+ rejection of 99.3%, a separation factor of 52.8, and a permeation flux of 21.1 LMH. During the 120 h continuous-filtration test, the Mg2+ rejection remained above 98.9%, while the Mg2+/Li+ mass ratio in the permeate was maintained at 0.28–0.40. The membrane also exhibited a good antifouling performance.

works.title: Dual-Regulation of Interfacial Polymerization via Interlayer and Surfactant: Molecular Dynamics Insights and High-Performance Mg2+/Li+ Separation Nanofiltration Membrane
institutions: Institute of New Functional Materials of Guangxi Institute of Industrial Technology , ,
works.abstract: Abstract A polyamide nanofiltration (NF) membrane with high permeance and Mg2+/Li+ selectivity was developed through a dual regulation strategy combining a tannic acid (TA) and Al3+ coordination interlayer with sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS). Molecular dynamics simulations showed that surfactant structure significantly affects the interaction and molecular mobility of polyethylenimine (PEI), with SDS providing effective regulation of PEI transport behavior. The TA and Al3+ coordination interlayer regulates PEI retention and local supply near the substrate surface, while SDS modulates PEI molecular mobility, providing complementary regulation of interfacial polymerization. Structural characterization showed that the dual regulation strategy promoted the formation of a thin and hydrophilic polyamide selective layer and decreased the proportion of surface carboxyl groups from 23.51% for the pristine PA membrane to 13.36% for the TA-Al3+/PA-SDS membrane, resulting in favorable surface charge characteristics. The optimized membrane exhibited a MgCl2 rejection of 99.26%, a LiCl rejection of 32.9%, an Mg2+/Li+ separation factor of 44.36, and a water permeance of 10.21 L·m−2·h−1·bar−1. The membrane also maintained relatively stable separation performance during 72 h filtration. These results demonstrate that coordinated regulation of PEI supply and molecular mobility provides an effective strategy for constructing high performance NF membranes for Mg2+/Li+ separation and lithium recovery from brines.

works.title: Interfacially Regulated MXene‐Based Nanocomposite Membranes for Highly Selective Ion Transport and Salinity Gradient Energy Harvesting
institutions: Center for Membranes and Advanced Water Technology (CMAT) Khalifa University of Science and Technology Abu Dhabi UAE
Department of Chemical and Petroleum Engineering Khalifa University of Science and Technology Abu Dhabi UAE
Khalifa University of Science and Technology Abu Dhabi UAE

Sustainable and Resilient Materials Lab Center for Integrative Petroleum Research (CIPR) College of Petroleum Engineering and Geosciences (CPG) King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals (KFUPM) Dhahran Saudi Arabia
Department of Materials Science and Engineering Drexel University Philadelphia Pennsylvania USA
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving high ion selectivity, low membrane resistance, and long‐term stability remains a key challenge in developing two‐dimensional nanomaterial polymer composite membranes, where interfacial interactions critically influence membrane structure and ion transport. Here, we report interfacially regulated MXene‐based nanocomposite membranes in which humic acid (HA) mediates interactions between Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene nanosheets and a sulfonated polyethersulfone matrix. Structural characterization together with molecular dynamics simulations indicates that HA incorporation modifies MXene organization and interfacial interactions within the membrane, which are associated with enhanced ion‐transport properties. The optimized membrane achieved near‐ideal monovalent cation selectivity (∼99%), a low area‐specific membrane resistance of 0.06 Ω·m 2 , and an energy conversion efficiency of 45.6%. The same membrane was evaluated over multiple electrochemical testing cycles totaling approximately 300 h, including dedicated 48 h stability measurements under heavy‐metal‐ and organic‐foulant‐containing conditions. A model‐based assessment of a conceptual reverse electrodialysis (RED) stack predicts a 37% increase in power generation, accompanied by an increase in energy conversion efficiency from 30.0% to 41.1%, relative to the commercial‐membrane scenario. These findings demonstrate that regulating interfacial interactions provides an effective design strategy for developing MXene‐based ion‐selective membranes for salinity‐gradient energy harvesting and related electrochemical separation processes.

works.title: Hydrophobic materials for hydrophobic membrane engineering
works.abstract: Hydrophobic materials have become increasingly important for separation technologies operating under humid or chemically aggressive conditions, where conventional membranes often suffer from performance degradation. This review summarizes recent advances in hydrophobic membranes based on fluoropolymers, graphitic materials, zeolites, and porous crystalline frameworks, including metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), covalent organic frameworks (COFs), and hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (HOFs). The roles of surface hydrophobicity, pore structure, and interfacial interactions in controlling transport, selectivity, and stability are critically discussed across applications in water treatment, organic solvent nanofiltration, gas separation, air purification, and energy-related systems. Representative examples highlight how hydrophobic interfaces mitigate water-induced swelling, pore blocking, and competitive adsorption, thereby enabling stable and efficient separations. Despite substantial progress, challenges remain in scalable fabrication, long-term stability, and cost-effective production, particularly for framework-based membranes. Future directions toward hybrid architectures, defect and interface engineering, and scalable processing are outlined to facilitate the translation of hydrophobic membrane materials into industrially relevant separation technologies.

works.title: Chalcogen‐Bond‐Driven Electrochemical Bromide Sequestration in Benzothiazole‐Functionalized Covalent Organic Frameworks
institutions: Department of Chemistry Khalifa University of Science & Technology Abu Dhabi UAE
Center For Catalysis & Separations (CeCaS) Khalifa University of Science & Technology Abu Dhabi UAE
CATS Research Group, School of Chemical Sciences and Engineering Yachay Tech University Urcuqui Ecuador
Mechanical and Nuclear Engineering Department Khalifa University of Science and Technology Abu Dhabi UAE
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Bromide contamination in water sources is a growing health concern because it can generate carcinogenic disinfection byproducts during conventional water treatment. However, the selective removal of bromide from reverse osmosis (RO) permeate remains challenging. Herein, we report a benzothiazole‐functionalized covalent organic framework (COF) designed as a chalcogen‐bond donor, where σ‐holes along the C─S bond axes preferentially interact with the softer, more polarizable Br − over Cl − . Two COFs, mesoporous BTzTp (∼2.45 nm) and microporous TTzTp (∼1.13 nm), were investigated to assess the role of pore accessibility while preserving identical recognition sites. The BTzTp@rGO composite exhibited a specific capacitance of 47 F g − 1 and a maximum bromide adsorption capacity of 36.7 mg‐Br − g − 1 at pH 4. Notably, it maintained ∼99% capacitance retention after 50 cycles, representing the highest cycling stability reported for a bromide‐selective HCDI electrode, together with excellent selectivity (α Br/Cl = 10). Density functional theory calculations reveal that selectivity originates from strong chalcogen bonding, evidenced by near‐linear C─S···Br − geometries (178°–179°), normalized contacts of 0.84, HOMO delocalization across the S···Br − interface, and greater charge transfer to Br − (0.222 e) than Cl − (0.154 e). This work demonstrates a viable strategy for highly selective and stable bromide removal in energy‐efficient water purification systems.

works.title: Polymer-modified MXene thin-film nanocomposite membranes for forward osmosis
works.abstract: Abstract Water scarcity demands novel solutions to address the challenges posed by increasing societal needs. This study presents a novel strategy for fabricating MXene-based thin-film nanocomposite forward osmosis (TFN-FO) membranes with enhanced permeability and selectivity, offering a promising advancement in water treatment technologies. The approach involves synthesizing MXene-functionalized polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP-g-MXene) additives through a facile chemical grafting method, where hydroxyl groups serve as linkers to covalently bond PVP onto the surface of 2D MXene nanosheets. Subsequently, PVP-g-MXene is incorporated into a polyamide (PA) thin film via interfacial polymerization (IP) to produce the innovative TFN-FO membranes. Characterization of MXene and PVP-g-MXene was performed using FT-IR, XRD, TGA, and FE-SEM. The fabricated membranes were analyzed for surface morphology, roughness, and hydrophilicity using FESEM, AFM, and water contact angle (WCA) measurements. The results indicate that incorporating PVP-g-MXene significantly alters the physicochemical properties of the membranes, including morphology, roughness, hydrophilicity, and overall performance during the IP process. All modified membranes demonstrated improved water flux compared to the pristine TFC membrane, with TFN-PgM1 and TFN-PgM2 exhibiting superior selectivity. Notably the representative TFN-PgM2 membrane exhibited a water flux of 18.5 LMH, which is approximately 72% higher than that of the TFC membrane, and demonstrated a Js/Jw ratio of 0.167, indicating an 18.1% improvement in selectivity performance. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of polymer-modified MXene for the development of high-performance FO membranes.

works.title: Dual-Layer Architecture in Hollow Fiber Membranes for Enhanced H2, CO2, and SF6 Separation
institutions: CSIR-North East Institute of Science and Technology , , , ,
Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research (AcSIR) , , ,
works.abstract: Abstract The growing demand for efficient hydrogen purification and the recovery of high-global-warming-potential gases has intensified the development of compact, energy-efficient membrane processes for industrial gas separation. Composite hollow fiber membranes (HFMs) provide an effective platform for integrating a multilayer structure of a porous substrate and a thin selective layer. However, the applicability of multilayer polymeric HFMs beyond conventional CO2 capture systems remains underexplored, particularly for gas pairs with different molecular sizes. In this study, a dual-layer PES/PDMS/PEBAX-1657 HFM comprising a PES substrate, an ultrathin PDMS gutter layer (∼85 nm), and a PEBAX-1657 selective layer (∼150 nm) was fabricated via sequential coating and investigated for the separation of H2, CO2, N2, and SF6. The performance of the membrane was evaluated using H2, CO2, N2, and SF6 as molecularly distinct probe gases over a pressure range of 1–5 bar. The PES/PDMS/PEBAX-1657 membrane exhibited H2, CO2, N2, and SF6 permeances of 140.82, 71.87, 25.02, and 16.56 GPU, respectively, at 30 °C and 5 bar. This work establishes the PES/PDMS/PEBAX-1657 HFMs as a versatile platform for fundamentally different gas-separation systems, rather than being introduced solely for CO2 capture/hydrogen purification. The combination of high gas permeance and a mechanically robust hollow fiber configuration offers potential for high-throughput operation with reduced membrane-area requirements, while selective-layer and interfacial engineering provide scope for further enhancement of separation selectivity. These findings establish the PES/PDMS/PEBAX-1657 structure as a promising multilayer HFM platform for hydrogen recovery and SF6 separation in electrical power industry applications.

works.title: Boron nitride nanosheets filtration membrane for efficient separation of pollutant molecules from aqueous solution
institutions: State Key Laboratory of Advanced Separation Membrane Materials
works.abstract: Two dimensional nanomaterials have exhibit promising performance in membrane science, especially hexagonal boron nitride nanosheets (BNNSs) with inherent chemical inertness. Here, BNNSs membranes with compact and well-organized stacking texture were successfully prepared via vacuum-assisted filtration approach using chemo-mechanical exfoliated and functionalized BNNSs as matrix. The BNNSs with an average lateral dimension of ~100 nm have few layers structure and abundant hydroxyl and amino groups. The viscosity of the solvent and thickness of membrane are important factors affecting the permeability performance. Importantly, the BNNSs membranes exhibit fascinating filtration and separation performance for various pollutants in water, including abusive organic dyes, heavy metal ion and drugs. Specifically, the membrane with a typical thickness of 30 μm shows the water flux up to 2.1 L⋅m −2 ⋅min −1 ⋅bar −1 and 99.87% removal rate for tetracycline. These performances are not only caused by simple physical interception of BNNSs constructed nanochannels, but also by certain intermolecular chemical interactions between functional groups on BNNSs and pollutant molecules. This work would provide experimental foundation and analytical experience for the practical application of BNNSs membranes in the field of complex water purification.

works.title: Water at the Interface: How Membrane Charge Controls Nanoplastic–Lipid Interactions
works.journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
works.abstract: Abstract Nanoplastics are pervasive environmental contaminants capable of crossing biological barriers and interacting with cell membranes. However, the molecular mechanisms by which they perturb lipid interfaces remain poorly understood. Here, we combine Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), ultrafast two-dimensional infrared spectroscopy (2D IR), and surface-enhanced infrared absorption (SEIRA) spectroscopy to investigate how anionic polystyrene nanoplastic (NP) particles modulate the environment at the lipid–water interface in model lipid membranes by varying composition and ionic environment. Neutral phosphatidylcholine (POPC) and anionic phosphatidylcholine/phosphatidylserine (POPC/POPS) membranes were used to probe the role of membrane charge on NP-induced interfacial perturbations. FTIR measurements show that NP-induced dehydration of the lipid headgroup region depends strongly on membrane composition, with partial dehydration observed in neutral POPC membranes but negligible changes in anionic POPC/POPS membranes. 2D IR spectra show that NPs induce faster H-bond fluctuations, as water molecules become more labile at the interface. SEIRA measurements further show that these interfacial perturbations are accompanied by localized changes in the acyl-chain ordering. Addition of Ca2+ enhances NP-induced changes to the negatively charged membranes, resulting in hydration dynamics and acyl-chain ordering that resemble those observed in neutral POPC membranes. These results are consistent with the hypothesis that interfacial dehydration is an early event associated with NP-membrane interactions and highlight the role of membrane charge and ionic environment in modulating these interactions.

works.title: Review on Thermal Vacuum Desalination: Technologies, Challenges and Sustainable Pathways
institutions: Mechanical Engineering Department, King Fahd University of Petroleum & Minerals, Dhahran 31261, Saudi Arabia
Interdisciplinary Research Center for Sustainable Energy Systems (IRC-SES), King Fahd University of Petroleum & Minerals, Dhahran 31261, Saudi Arabia
works.abstract: Global water scarcity and the energy demand of conventional desalination motivate the development of thermal vacuum desalination (VD), which lowers the boiling temperature of saline water and can use low-grade heat from solar, waste-heat, ocean-thermal, and geothermal sources. This review traces the progression from passive natural-vacuum systems to forced-vacuum, ejector, spray-flash, falling-film, and membrane configurations. Reported headline values are case-specific. A reviewed multistage solar natural-vacuum configuration reported thermal efficiency up to 86%, and one experimental variable-geometry radial ejector reported an average entrainment-ratio improvement of 107% relative to its tested reference geometry. An experimental solar Venturi prototype produced 7.01–9.02 kg/(m2·d), depending on its operating cycle. Separately, a validated Aspen Plus simulation of a 14-effect MED-HV system reported a GOR of 13.49, while an experimental DCMD-crystallization study reported 98.9% water recovery for hypersaline produced water. Despite these promising results, the large-scale deployment of vacuum desalination technologies remains hindered by operational instabilities, intermittent thermal inputs, and membrane scaling. This review critically evaluates vacuum desalination technologies by distinguishing modeled, laboratory, pilot-scale, and review-derived evidence. It assesses energy consumption, techno-economic feasibility, and environmental performance on a case-specific basis. This review highlights major challenges in vacuum desalination (VD), such as vacuum stability, intermittent operation, scaling, irreversible membrane wetting, and long-term performance validation, and suggests research priorities for the future. Through this assessment of key findings, this review outlines a strategic approach to advancing thermal VD technologies toward sustainable, practical applications by integrating water treatment, energy efficiency, and mineral recovery through water–energy–mineral synergies.

works.title: Geopolymer-based materials for CO₂/CH₄ separation and H₂S capture: Current evidence, limitations, and research needs
works.abstract: Efficient biogas upgrading requires the removal of CO₂ and H₂S to produce biomethane suitable for downstream applications. Geopolymer-based materials have attracted interest because their aluminosilicate structures can be tailored through precursor composition, activation, curing, and secondary-phase incorporation, while waste-derived precursors offer opportunities for resource valorization. This review critically evaluates geopolymer-based CO₂/CH₄ separation and H₂S capture and examines their potential integration into a single membrane platform. The literature provides limited direct evidence of CO₂/CH₄ separation using geopolymer membranes, whereas CO₂/CH₄ adsorption selectivity has been demonstrated in geopolymer-based materials, and H₂S capture has primarily been investigated using particulate or bulk geopolymer sorbents. However, the available literature has yet to establish the integrated performance of a single geopolymer membrane for CO₂/CH₄ separation and H₂S removal under mixed CO₂/CH₄/H₂S feeds. Consequently, the existing evidence remains fragmented across adsorption, gas permeation, and H₂S sorption studies. Key research gaps include establishing the relationship between adsorption properties and membrane-level separation, controlling selective-layer thickness and defects, elucidating gas transport mechanisms, and validating performance under humid, multicomponent conditions. The review also examines membrane architecture, functionalization, composite design, and emerging metal–organic framework (MOF) and covalent organic framework (COF) systems to identify relevant design principles. Altogether, integrated CO₂/CH₄/H₂S purification using geopolymer membranes remains largely at the proof-of-concept stage. Future research should prioritize mixed-gas testing, H₂S breakthrough and regeneration studies, interface engineering, and standardized transport measurements.

works.title: Photothermal Evaporator with MXene‐Regulated Fe <sup>3+</sup> /Fe <sup>2+</sup> Cycling via Ligand‐to‐Metal Charge Transfer for Solar Desalination and Wastewater Purification
institutions: School of Textile Science & Engineering Xi′an Polytechnic University Xi′an Shaanxi China
Key Laboratory of Functional Textile Material and Product Ministry of Education (Xi'an Polytechnic University) Xi'an Shaanxi China
Key Laboratory of Functional Clothing Fabric of Shaanxi Province Xi'an Polytechnic University Xi'an Shaanxi China
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Combining interfacial solar evaporation and advanced oxidation provides a promising approach to ease global energy shortages and water pollution. However, fabricating bifunctional evaporators with excellent photothermal, catalytic and synergistic properties remains a tough technical challenge. In this work, a glass fiber membrane was adopted as the functional substrate to anchor MXene/MIL‐101(Fe) composites, thereby constructing a bifunctional evaporator (M/T‐GFM) integrating photothermal and catalytic capacities. As a photothermal component, MXene captures solar light and converts light energy into thermal energy to boost peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation. Meanwhile, MXene acts as an electron donor to accelerate the Fe 3+ /Fe 2+ redox cycle within MIL‐101(Fe) via ligand‐to‐metal charge transfer (LMCT). It takes merely 20 min to degrade high‐concentration Reactive Blue 19 (R.B.19) of 100 mg L −1 completely and 84.32% of phenol in the condensed water, while the water evaporation rate hits 2.49 kg m −2 h −1 . Meanwhile, it exhibits excellent purification on actual dyeing and finishing wastewater. Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations clarify PMS activation over Fe‐O‐Ti and Fe‐O sites. Relying on the synergistic mechanism where MXene‐mediated photothermal conversion and LMCT accelerate the Fe 3+ /Fe 2+ redox cycle, this study provides a new strategy for concurrent freshwater generation and wastewater remediation combining interfacial evaporation and a PMS based advanced oxidation process.

works.title: Toward Low-Carbon Seawater Desalination: Integrating Thermal and Membrane Technologies, Renewable Energy, and AI Optimization with Life-Cycle Assessment
institutions: Department of Civil Engineering, University of Alaska Anchorage, Anchorage, AK 99508, USA
Arcadis US Inc., 222 S Main St., Suite 200, Akron, OH 44308, USA
Department of Chemical Engineering, Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology, Dhaka 1000, Bangladesh
Department of Chemical Engineering, Virginia Tech, Blacksburg, VA 24061, USA
Bangladesh Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority, Dhaka 1207, Bangladesh
Arcadis US Inc., 2839 Paces Ferry Rd SE #1000, Atlanta, GA 30339, USA
Ivory V. Nelson Center for the Sciences, Department of Chemistry and Physics, Lincoln University, 1570 Baltimore Pike, Oxford, PA 19352, USA
Department of Textile Engineering, Faculty of Engineering, Daffodil International University, Dhaka 1216, Bangladesh
works.abstract: Seawater desalination can only be sustainable if it cuts energy use, membrane fouling, brine discharge, and water cost. This review compares thermal and membrane technologies against these four challenges. RO supplies 70 to 80% of desalinated water at 3 to 5.5 kWh/m3, against 6.5 to 12 for MED and vapor compression and 13.5 to 25.5 for MSF, and it usually gives the lowest water cost, though energy prices and brine rules shift this. Thermal processes still yield purer distillate. A life-cycle appraisal structured by ISO 14040 and 14044 finds that energy drives most RO emissions, that brine recovery lowers impacts, and that low-carbon heat or different criteria weights can reverse technology rankings. Hybrids target recovery and scaling: RO–MSF and NF–RO have commercial or pilot cases, whereas MSF–MED and MD-based options rest on simulations and pilot work. AI models now optimize energy use, forecast fouling, and monitor water quality, but rarely link thermal, brine, and life-cycle stages. Priorities are fouling-resistant membranes, renewable-powered hybrids, brine minimization, and joint AI and life-cycle assessment.

works.title: Bioinspired Adaptive Ångström‐Channels in a Hydrogen‐Bonded Metal–Organic Framework for Selective Water Removal From Gas Streams by Molecular Sieving Dehydration
institutions: Key Laboratory of the Ministry of Education for Advanced Catalysis Materials Zhejiang Key Laboratory of Advanced Catalysis and Adsorption Materials, College of Chemistry and Materials Science Zhejiang Normal University Jinhua P. R. China
Institute of Advanced Fluorine‐Containing Materials Zhejiang Normal University Jinhua P. R. China
Fujian Provincial Key Laboratory of Polymer Materials, College of Chemistry & Materials Science Fujian Normal University Fuzhou P. R. China
works.abstract: ABSTRACT The removal of water from light hydrocarbons is a critical yet energy‐intensive step in petrochemical processes. Conventional adsorbents often suffer from high regeneration temperatures and undesirable co‐adsorption. Inspired by the selective water transport mechanism of aquaporins, we report a hydrogen‐bonded metal–organic framework, ZNU‐33, featuring bioinspired adaptive one‐dimensional channels. The pore walls are decorated with both positively charged (Hbpa + ) and negatively charged (HEDP 4− ) recognition sites. Using in situ single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction, we captured five phases of ZNU‐33, activated (ZNU‐33‐α), intermediate (ZNU‐33‐β), partially dehydrated (ZNU‐33‐γ and ZNU‐33‐γ2), and fully hydrated ZNU‐33, directly visualizing a water‑triggered structural transition. Structural snapshots reveal water uptake proceeding from free‐channel water to Cu 2+ coordination and then to extended hydrogen‐bonded water chains. ZNU‐33 exhibits high water uptake (9.50 mmol/g at 2.85 kPa and 298 K) and negligible adsorption of CO 2 and all light hydrocarbons. Breakthrough experiments demonstrate efficient water removal under wide flow rates, temperatures, and humidity levels, with water‐adsorption capacity recoverable under substantially milder activation conditions than those required by the investigated conventional zeolites. This work not only provides a high‑performance material for selective dehydration, but also establishes a bioinspired adaptive adsorption mechanism for designing water‐selective adsorbents.

works.title: Advancing Lithium Recovery: Evaluation of Electrodialysis, Capacitive Deionization, and a Hybrid Electrochemical System
institutions: Kroll Institute for Extractive Metallurgy, Department of Minerals and Subsurface Energy, Colorado School of Mines, Golden, CO 80401, USA
works.abstract: Because of the increasing demand for lithium, interest has grown in developing highly efficient methods to separate lithium from non-conventional sources such as lithium clays. This study assesses electrodialysis (EDU) and capacitive deionization (CDI), as well as a combined EDU–CDI method, for recovering and purifying lithium from a chloride-containing leachate solution obtained from lithium clays. This study examined the initial stage of the EDU process. Under different conditions (voltage, treatment time, and flow rates), the concentration depletion and enrichment of lithium, as well as its recovery and selectivity, were investigated. All electrochemical experiments were conducted at ambient laboratory temperature. CDI was examined as a polishing technique, with particular attention to lithium recovery and discrimination between Li+ and Na+ ions using modified carbon-based electrodes. The results show that the EDU technique can promote lithium transport and enrichment; however, Li/Na selectivity remains low because the monovalent ions are transported simultaneously. The CDI technique has demonstrated a greater degree of lithium enrichment compared to that of Na+ ions, which shows its potential as a selective separation step. When combined, the techniques show complementary effects: EDU performs bulk ion separation, while CDI improves the quality of the lithium-enriched solution. Furthermore, preliminary tests have indicated promising behavior of the LiMn2O4-based electrodes.

works.title: Antimicrobial Evaluation of WO₃–TiO₂ Nanocomposites Against Pathogenic Bacterial and Fungal Strains.
works.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
works.abstract: In this study, WO3/TiO2 nanocomposites were synthesized and thermally calcined at 800℃ and 1200℃ to evalute the effect of calcination on structural, optical and antimicrobial perfromance. XRD and FTIR confirmed the formation of mixed-phase crystalline frameworks, while UV-Vis spectroscopy revealed strong visible-light absorption and Tauc plot analysis indicated reduced band gap energies, enhancing antibacterial and antifungal activity. HR-SEM micrograph showed unifromly dispersion spherical nanoparticles with narrow size distribution and minimal agglomeration. The antimicrobial activity of WO₃, TiO₂, and their WO₃/TiO₂ nanocomposites was evaluated against both bacterial and fungal strains. The WO₃/TiO₂ nanocomposites exhibited excellent antibacterial and antifungal activities, with the sample calcined at 1200°C showing significantly higher inhibition zones than the 800°C sample against both bacterial and fungal pathogens. Candida albicans was more susceptible than Aspergillus niger, while strong antibacterial activity was observed against both Gram-positive and Gramnegative bacteria. The enhanced antimicrobial performance is attributed to improved crystallinity, efficient interfacial charge transfer, and increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, resulting in effective disruption of microbial cell membranes. These findings demonstrate that WO₃/TiO₂ nanocomposites are promising eco-friendly materials for antimicrobial coatings, environmental disinfection, and water purification applications.

works.title: Long‐Lifespan Polyorganosiloxane‐Based Silicone Evaporator for High‐Efficiency Seawater Desalination
institutions: College of Materials Engineering Fujian Agriculture and Forestry University Fuzhou People's Republic of China
College of Materials and Chemical Engineering Minjiang University Fuzhou Fujian China
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional evaporators suffer from poor mechanical strength, salt crystallization, and degradation in sea water. We design a white polyorganosiloxane‐based solar evaporator (PDMSE) that exploits siliconeʼs unique attributes. These include chemical inertness, anti‑corrosion, high flexibility, and chemical resistance. Such characteristics ensure structural integrity and anti‑fouling performance under harsh brine conditions. The white surface combined with a reflector enables efficient light scattering and heat localization. Reflector‐equipped PDMSE achieves evaporation rates of 4.344 kg m −2 h −1 at 1 sun and 8.087 kg m −2 h −1 at 3 suns in 3.5 wt.% NaCl. It shows no salt accumulation over 8 h operation and maintains stable cycling for 53 days. Moreover, PDMSE withstands seawater immersion for 197 days without degradation. The evaporator also purifies sea water to World Health Organization drinking standards. This work provides a durable and scalable silicone‑based strategy for high‑performance desalination.

works.title: Bioinspired Self-Floating Hydrogel-Coated Foam for Synergistic Solar Power Generation and Desalination
institutions: Shenzhen Polytechnic University , 7098 Liuxian Avenue , Nanshan District, ,
works.abstract: Abstract Interfacial solar-driven evaporation provides a sustainable route for freshwater generation, but practical implementation remains limited by salt accumulation, insufficient understanding of water/ion transport, and inefficient utilization of the evaporated vapor. Herein, we report an interfacially engineered self-floating hydrogel-coated foam evaporator constructed by anchoring Ketjen black/sodium alginate/tannic acid/Fe3+ networks onto a melamine foam skeleton. The Fe3+ ions serve as multivalent coordination centers, simultaneously interacting with the carboxylate groups of sodium alginate and the phenolic groups of tannic acid, thereby forming a stable hydrophilic coating with enhanced surface wettability and robust interfacial adhesion. The open-cell macroporous foam provides low-resistance water supply pathways, while the hydrophilic hydrogel coating promotes surface-mediated water spreading and salt redissolution. Under 1 sun illumination, the optimized evaporator exhibits an evaporation rate of 3.56 kg m–2 h–1 and a solar-to-vapor efficiency of 92.4%. This performance is attributed to broadband solar absorption, localized heat management, and reduced effective evaporation enthalpy of interfacial water. The evaporator maintains stable evaporation in seawater for 120 h without obvious salt crystallization, mainly owing to capillary rewetting, concentration-gradient-driven ion diffusion, and density-driven brine exchange through the macroporous network. In addition, the device enables simultaneous hydrovoltaic electricity generation using inert electrodes. This work provides a chemically and structurally integrated strategy for solar desalination and water-enabled energy harvesting.

works.title: A Columnar Shear-Assisted Freeze Desalination System
institutions: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology , , Clear Water Bay ,
works.abstract: Abstract Freeze desalination is an emerging desalination technique. Previous studies showed that shear-assisted freeze desalination could achieve drinking water production through one freezing cycle. However, the productivity of this approach is relatively low and the energy consumption is relatively high. To address these drawbacks, we developed a columnar shear-assisted freeze desalination system, where seawater flows through a vertical tube with ice formed at the inner surface of the tube. At constant seawater flow rates, potable water is produced at high flow rates. Unfortunately, the drinking water productivity remains low (0.48 kg·m–2·h–1) and the energy consumption is high. By linearly lowering the seawater flow rate during freezing, the drinking water productivity reaches 2.28 kg·m–2·h–1, a 4.8-fold increase compared to the cases with constant flow rates, and the total specific energy consumption is significantly reduced from 11.64 to 1.20 kWh·kg–1. Experiments with natural seawater are also conducted. Due to the relatively low salinity of the natural seawater used (32.53 g·L–1), the productivity of drinking water and the total specific energy consumption reach 5.32 kg·m–2·h–1 and 0.83 kWh·kg–1, respectively. The results indicate that the proposed desalination system is promising for commercialization.

works.title: Nanomaterials for Water Purification Towards Global Water Crisis Sustainable Solutions
works.journal: Innovative Reviews in Engineering and Science
works.abstract: Providing the world's increasingly growing population with clean, affordable water is an unprecedented challenge for the 21st century. In the face of climate change and failing water quality, nanotechnology has become the center piece in innovation in this global crisis. This article discusses the ways in which nanomaterials are leading the way in the revolution of the water purification techniques and are providing sustainable means to increase access to safe drinking water around the world. Water scarcity and pollution threaten human health, economic development and environmental sustainability. Traditional water treatment methods do not generally achieve effective removal of emerging pollutants and pathogen. Thus, the properties of nanomaterials at the molecular scale make it unique, and open new possibilities for development of more efficient, cost effective and environmentally friendly water purification. Nanotechnology is changing the way we clean and reuse water resources from nano adsorbents that remove toxic metals selectively and nanomembranes that filter out the slightest contaminants. In this article we will look at the advances in nanomaterials for water purification looking at how they work, what they are good for, and they could help enlighten us about the global water crisis. Through these innovations we’ll explore ways these are redefining the future of water management for anyone and everyone, not just industries and communities, but all across the globe.

works.title: Microwave-Assisted Degradation of Unsaturated Polyester Resin into HDPE-Modified Aerogels for Oil Adsorption and Oil/Water Separation
institutions: Key Laboratory of Oil & Gas Fine Chemicals, Ministry of Education, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, School of Chemical Engineering, Xinjiang University, Urumqi 830017, China
School of Mechanical Engineering & Center for Post-Doctoral Studies of Mechanical Engineering, Xinjiang University, Urumqi 830017, China
works.abstract: Thermosetting unsaturated polyester resin (UPR) is difficult to reprocess because curing generates an irreversible three-dimensional network. Here, cured UPR was treated in a microwave-assisted hydrazine hydrate/NaOH medium at 70 °C for 30 min to produce a water-swellable UPR-derived product (NUPR). NUPR was combined with glutaraldehyde, subjected to freeze–thaw processing and freeze-drying, and subsequently modified with high-density polyethylene (HDPE) to fabricate porous aerogels. FTIR results were consistent with partial cleavage of ester-containing structures, while TGA and SEM revealed changes in thermal behavior and morphology. Among the tested aerogels, AAS-6 exhibited a density of approximately 0.036 g cm−3 and a porosity of 96.6%. After HDPE treatment, the aerogel exhibited a water contact angle of 135.2° while maintaining rapid oil wetting. Its 5 min liquid uptake for the tested oils and organic solvents ranged from 20.14 to 38.31 g g−1. After ten adsorption–regeneration cycles, 89–96% of the initial oil uptake was retained, depending on the oil, whereas uptake of the tested volatile solvents remained comparatively unchanged under the respective regeneration conditions. H-6 also enabled free-oil uptake from water and gravity-driven treatment of surfactant-stabilized water-in-oil (W/O) emulsions, yielding high separation efficiencies and markedly reduced dispersed-droplet signals after filtration. These results demonstrate a route for coupling the chemical conversion of cured UPR with fabrication of porous materials for oil uptake and W/O emulsion separation.

works.title: Catalytic Metal–Organic Framework Membranes: Advances in Electrocatalysis, Photocatalysis, and Thermocatalysis
institutions: Faculty of Arts and Sciences, Beijing Normal University, Zhuhai 519087, China
Center for Advanced Materials Research, Advanced Institute of Natural Sciences, Beijing Normal University, Zhuhai 519087, China
works.abstract: Metal–organic framework (MOF) membranes combine the structural designability of MOFs with a continuous membrane architecture that integrates reactant enrichment, active-site accessibility, and product separation. This review surveys catalytic MOF membranes reported from 2016 to 2025, from fabrication strategies—classified by how catalytic function is integrated with the membrane (intrinsic framework active sites, guest species incorporation, and non-catalytic microenvironment coating)—to catalytic performance in electrocatalysis, photocatalysis, and thermocatalysis. In electrocatalysis, non-catalytic MOF coatings improve CO2 reduction and nitrogen reduction, whereas MOF-derived electrodes currently lead water-splitting benchmarks. In photocatalysis, MOF membranes have enabled CO2 reduction with near-unity HCOOH selectivity, pollutant degradation, Cr(VI) reduction, and H2 evolution stable for over 1000 h. In thermocatalysis, membrane demonstrations are so far confined to low- and medium-temperature antibacterial and oxidative desulfurization applications, whereas alkyne semihydrogenation and high-temperature operation of intact membranes remain largely unexplored. Across all three regimes, membrane geometry governs reactant enrichment, separation, and catalyst recoverability, yet inconsistent reporting limits cross-study comparison. Key challenges and future directions are discussed.

works.title: Waste-Derived Zeolite-P (GIS): Synthesis, Polymorphism, Characterization, and Adsorption Applications for Water Purification and Selective Gas Separation
institutions: Laboratory of Applied Organic Synthesis, Faculty of Exact and Applied Sciences, University Oran1 Ahmed Ben Bella, BP 1524 El M’Naouer, Oran 31000, Algeria

Laboratory of Elaboration and Spectroscopic Characterizations of Structural and Electronic Properties Materials, Faculty of Technology, University of Saida Tahar Moulay University, P.B. 138 Ennasr, Saida 20000, Algeria
Qi S.r.l., Via Monte d’Oro, 2/A, 00071 Pomezia, Italy
Research Direction, Universidad ECOTEC, Km 13.5 Samborondón, Samborondón 092302, Ecuador
National Institute of Materials Physics (NIMP), 405A Atomistilor Street, 077125 Magurele, Romania
works.abstract: Zeolite-P is a synthetic member of the gismondine (GIS) framework family and is intrinsically microporous, with intersecting eight-membered-ring channels. Mesoporosity reported for some Zeolite-P samples is therefore a secondary textural feature arising from interparticle voids, crystal aggregation, defects, or deliberately hierarchical architectures rather than from the GIS framework itself. This critical review focuses specifically on waste-derived GIS/Zeolite-P and integrates polymorph selection (Na-P1 and Na-P2), phase-purity assessment, precursor-to-property relationships, shaping, regeneration, and adsorption under increasingly realistic conditions. Structural and compositional evidence from X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), X-ray fluorescence (XRF), inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES), solid-state 29Si and 27Al magic-angle-spinning nuclear magnetic resonance (MAS NMR), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) analysis is evaluated in terms of what each technique can establish specifically for GIS materials. Waste-derived synthesis routes—including hydrothermal, alkali-fusion-assisted, microwave-assisted, ultrasound-assisted, sol–gel, and solvent-free methods—are compared without assuming that a waste precursor or a shorter synthesis is intrinsically lower-impact. Particular attention is paid to water purification, ion exchange, dehydration, and selective gas adsorption, while distinguishing single-solute batch tests from multicomponent, real-water, regeneration, and breakthrough evidence. The review also reconciles computational predictions with experiments: idealized pure-silica GIS models can overpredict CO2 uptake relative to realistic aluminosilicate Na-P1/Na-P2, for which extra-framework cations, hydration, and restricted diffusion strongly affect accessibility. The resulting analysis identifies phase purity, matrix effects, regeneration, leaching safety, shaping, and process-level techno-economic/life-cycle metrics as the key barriers to translation of waste-derived Zeolite-P from laboratory studies to deployable adsorbents.

works.title: Development and Application of a High-Resolution Cryogenic STXM System at the Shanghai Synchrotron Radiation Facility
institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
works.abstract: Abstract Scanning transmission X-ray microscopy (STXM) is an advanced technique for label-free chemical imaging with nanometer-scale spatial resolution which is well suited to studies of complex and heterogeneous materials. For biological and other radiation-sensitive specimens, however, the X-ray dose required for high-quality imaging often exceeds the damage threshold of the sample at room temperature. The resulting mass loss, chemical modification, and structural collapse corrupt the very signals under investigation. Cryogenic sample conditions can mitigate these effects by suppressing radiation-induced diffusion and secondary reactions. Yet their practical implementation is challenging. An instrument must simultaneously maintain stable low-temperature operation, isolate vibrations, and transfer samples without contamination under high vacuum. Satisfying all of these demands at once is difficult. Herein, we report the development and commissioning of a dedicated cryogenic STXM system installed on the beamline BL08U1A of the Shanghai Synchrotron Radiation Facility (SSRF). The instrument combines a mechanically decoupled cryostat architecture with a closed-loop ultra-high vacuum cryo-transfer system. It achieves a spatial resolution better than 30 nm and a long-term thermal drift below 0.05 nm/min. Validation on poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) films shows that imaging at 120 K extends the critical radiation dose by a factor of ∼39 times compared with room temperature. Mass loss and secondary radical reactions are effectively suppressed. In situ imaging of frozen-hydrated mouse embryonic fibroblasts further resolves subcellular features such as filopodia, free from dehydration artifacts. Together, these results establish a robust platform for nondestructive, high-resolution chemical imaging of radiation-sensitive materials under near-physiological conditions, providing a foundation for correlative and multimodal studies of hydrated biological systems.
